newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Online objects to Telecom PTT Internet plan.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Online objects to Telecom PTT Internet plan.

text.p: Internet provider Swiss Online said Monday it has filed a complaint with the Federal Transport and Communications Ministry (EVED) alleging anti-competitive practice by Switzerland's publicly-held telecoms provider.
"We have lodged an official complaint with the EVED," Guenter Nierlich, chief executive of Swiss Online, told Reuters.
A spokeswoman for the ministry confirmed the complaint had been received but it still had to decide where the the issue would be dealt with.
The Swiss online complaint is separate from a case pending in the Swiss Federal Court involving similar issues, which is expected to take a long time to be resolved.

Nierlich told Reuters in May he thought the Telecom PTT was engaging in unfair practices by failing to divulge plans for the location of its so-called "Points of Presence" (POPs), dial-up points through which users gain access to the Internet.
No one at Telecom, which has not confirmed plans to install POPs, was available for comment.

Nierlich said the complaint did not involve the right of the public telecoms company to set up POPs. But he contended Telecom PTT has failed to provide enough information about the location of planned POPs to ensure a level playing field for competitors.
Swiss Online says knowing Telecom PTT's plans for location of its POPs would allow other services planning similar installations to reduce user charges. Swiss Online plans to install 26 POPs.

Swiss cartel authorities said in May they found the Swiss public telecoms provider had operated at an unfair advantage when its set up its Internet service Blue Window in September. But it said the problems had been addressed.
At the time Telecom PTT denied any unfair practices and rejected the findings of the cartel office.
Swiss Online estimated the domestic market comprised roughly 250,000 Internet customers, adding that its own share of the market was roughly 145,000 customers.
